youtube_title: The Black Friday Playbook for Shopify Brands
title: The Black Friday Playbook for Shopify Brands: Profit, Not Just Orders
meta_title: Black Friday Playbook for Shopify: The Profit Grid
meta_description: Learn which Black Friday playbook fits your Shopify store, how to calculate your break-even discount, and the setup to run before November 23.
teaser: Two questions put your store in one of four Black Friday playbooks that protect profit instead of just chasing orders.
summary: A 30% Black Friday discount can mean you need twice the orders just to make the same profit, so the right Black Friday plan for a Shopify store depends on two questions: do your customers buy again, and can your margin take a discount? The answers put you in one of four boxes (the Comeback, the Rush, the Stack or the Vault), each with its own moves, and every store should add early access and treat returning customers differently from new ones.
key_takeaways: Run the break-even multiplier before you pick a discount: your margin divided by (your margin minus the discount) tells you how many times more orders you need just to stand still. Above 60% margin you have room, below 50% you don't.

If customers buy again and your margin has room, give every Black Friday order a January code (for example $20 off your next order over $80, valid January 5 to 31) so you have a reason to email them in your slowest month.
If your margin is thin, give away value instead of price: a free gift the customer sees as $30 but costs you maybe $8 beats 10% more off, which is $10 straight out of your margin.

Add an early access sign-up form now and give that list access 24 to 48 hours before everyone else. Klaviyo reported Scuffers' early access email made around 400% more revenue than the same email sent to everyone else.

Use Shopify's discount eligibility setting to give customers who have purchased at least once an extra gift or extra 5%, and send new visitors from ads straight to a best seller with the sale price showing.

Before Black Friday: show the price after discount with a crossed-out compare-at price, use automatic discounts, turn off your welcome pop-up, test-order every offer, and freeze your site from November 23.
Change your abandoned cart flow to send after 30 minutes and allow it once a day per customer. Little Sleepies made more on day one than they projected for the entire week.

sections.heading: How many more orders do you need to break even on a Black Friday discount?

blocks.text: If you give 30% off on Black Friday, you can need **twice the orders to make the same amount of profit**. It's a simple calculation, and most ecommerce brands never make it. They default to a bigger discount and judge the weekend on orders.
A bigger discount isn't the answer anyway. Klaviyo data shows that last year discounts went down, but sales went up 11%. So before you set any offer, answer two questions.

items: Do your customers buy again? Coffee beans, underwear and skincare: yes. A sofa, a stroller or a mattress: no.

Can your margin take a discount? Use the **break-even multiplier**: your margin divided by your margin minus the discount. That number is how many times more orders you need just to stand still. Rule of thumb: above 60% margin you have room, below 50% you don't.

blocks.text: Those two answers give you four boxes. I call it the **Black Friday Profit Grid**.

items: **The Comeback** (buy again, room in the margin): you win them now and earn in January.
**The Rush** (buy once, room in the margin): you win on the first order.
**The Stack** (buy again, thin margin): you add value instead of discount.
**The Vault** (buy once, thin margin): you sell access, not price.

sections.heading: The Comeback: how to turn Black Friday buyers into repeat customers

blocks.text: In the Comeback box, people purchase again and your margin has room. Black Friday is where you acquire the customer, and you expect them to come back later. There are three moves.

**Move one: discount the first order to get the repeat purchase.** A big discount gets people in the door, and if your product is one they get hooked on, they come back, whether that's a subscription or a one-time purchase.

**Move two: the January code.** Every Black Friday order gets a code that only works from January 5 to January 31. Something like $20 off your next order over $80. January is your slowest month, so now you have a reason to email every Black Friday buyer and they have a reason to come back. This isn't new: Kohl's has done it for years with spend $50, get $10 to use later.

**Move three: split your follow-up.** In one study, only 4% of new Black Friday customers ever bought again. New buyers should get the January code plus an email on how to get the most out of what they bought. Returning buyers get a loyalty perk.

sections.heading: The Rush: how to make Black Friday profitable when customers only buy once

blocks.text: In the Rush, people order once and your margin has room. There is no second order, so **you have to make the profit today, in that single order**.
**Move one: a hero product.** Take one of your best sellers and give it a big discount. That gets people in the door. Everything else is also discounted for Black Friday, but much less.
**Move two: tiered discounts with a visible progress bar.** Tiers only work if shoppers can see them, so add a progress bar to your cart, like "$40 more to unlock 30%".

This is also where the cart trick comes in, and it works in any of the four boxes: **keep the cart clean**. We tested a decluttered cart for a client, took out the extra upsell blocks, and conversion went up 11% over 3 months. That's about $41,000 in additional revenue. One progress bar beats four widgets.

**Move three: the mystery box.** Goose and Gander did this: three surprise items, and one is always their famous t-shirt. Customers get the surprise, you clear low stock, and your best sellers never get discounted.

Whatever box you're in, don't judge Black Friday on conversion rate. We use what we call the **visitor P&L**. Every discount you give away is profit margin you don't get back, so we look at what each visitor actually earns you. Profit is what matters, not the conversion rate or even the revenue.

sections.heading: The Stack: what to offer on Black Friday when your margins are thin

blocks.text: The Stack is for stores where customers buy again but margins are thin. Here you don't want to give more discount. Instead of giving away price, you **give away value** on the order.

items: **A free gift instead of a bigger discount.** Spend $100, get a product worth $30. The customer sees $30, but you pay maybe $8 to make it. Compare that to 10% more off, which is $10 straight out of your margin.
**A gift card bonus.** Buy a $100 gift card, get a $20 bonus card that only works from January. You get the cash in November and the customer back in January. Some gift cards are never even used.

**Free shipping instead of deeper discounts.** Lower your free shipping threshold for the weekend or make shipping free on everything. For a lot of shoppers, free shipping beats an extra 5% off, and on a big order it costs you less than 5%.

sections.heading: The Vault: what should premium brands with thin margins do on Black Friday?

blocks.text: The Vault is the toughest box: thin margins and single purchases. This is where discounting is the worst thing you can do. Instead of giving away price or value, you **give away access**. If you're a premium brand in any of the four boxes, these moves apply to you too.

**Move one: create something unique for Black Friday.** A limited product, a special variation or a color. It creates urgency because people want it, it runs out, and it ends after a set number of days, so you don't need to give anything away.

**Move two: password-only early access.** Some brands lock the whole store for a day and only the early access list gets in. It feels exclusive, but a password page blocks Google and breaks every ad pointing at your site. Only do this with a big, engaged list, and only for 24 hours, not the whole weekend.
**Move three: opt out completely.** REI has closed its stores on Black Friday since 2015. Patagonia once ran a Black Friday ad that said "Don't buy this jacket".
From a premium brand, saying no to Black Friday is a campaign in itself.

sections.heading: How do you set up Black Friday early access on Shopify?

blocks.text: Whatever box you're in, two steps come first. I call them the Head Start. Last Black Friday, revenue from returning customers grew 13.5% faster than revenue from new ones, and in one study only 4% of new Black Friday customers ever bought again. **Your best Black Friday customers are the ones you already have.** So let them in first.

Early access is the most proven tactic there is. Klaviyo published a case on the fashion brand Scuffers: last Black Friday, their early access email made around 400% more revenue than the same email sent to everyone else. If you do one thing this week, set this up.

items: Add an early access sign-up form to your website and ask for email address and phone number.
Give that list VIP access 48 to 24 hours before everyone else, while all your products and variants are still in stock.

Give them a better reason than "be the first". Some brands show new arrivals you can only see after you sign in, and make that visible now. The products are right there, you just can't see them yet, so curiosity builds your list.
Fill the list from Instagram: Klaviyo can reply to anyone who comments a keyword (say "early") with a DM and a sign-up link. It's free.
Put the sign-up on your order confirmation page too.

sections.heading: How should you treat returning customers differently on Black Friday?

blocks.text: On Black Friday you have two people on your store: someone who has already bought from you three times, and someone who clicked an ad for a big discount. Most stores show them exactly the same thing, and **that is costing you real dollars**.

Your returning customers already trust you, so give them something new visitors don't get. Shopify lets you limit a discount to one customer segment: go to Discounts, create one, and under Eligibility pick customers who have purchased at least once. Now your regulars get an extra gift or an extra 5%, and nobody else does.

New visitors need proof: your best sellers, your reviews and your guarantee right at the top. For ad traffic, skip the homepage and send people straight to the best seller with the sale price already showing.

The same goes for email. Shinola didn't email everyone harder. They sent Black Friday emails to their most engaged customers and SMS only to people who had engaged recently. Fewer people, and Klaviyo reported their Black Friday revenue went up 27%, with revenue per person emailed up 48%.

sections.heading: Black Friday checklist for Shopify stores

blocks.text: None of this works if your site and email aren't ready. Run these five checks before the sale.

items: **Show the price after discount, not just a percentage.** Set the compare-at price so the old price shows crossed out, and use automatic discounts instead of only codes. A coupon field is a door out of your checkout.
**Turn off your welcome pop-up.** "Sign up and get 10%" is irrelevant when you have a bigger sale running. Turn off any other campaigns too.

**Shopify Plus: check your Scripts.** Shopify Scripts stopped working on June 30th. If your tiered discounts or free gifts ran on Scripts, they're gone. Place a test order for every single offer before Monday the 21st.

**Freeze your site from November 23rd.** No new themes, go into a code freeze. A/B tests can stay live because they sit on top of your site and can be switched off easily, but avoid big risks during your most important week.

**Fix your abandoned cart timing.** Little Sleepies, a baby clothing brand, sent their abandoned cart email after 30 minutes instead of an hour, and let a customer receive it once a day instead of once every two weeks. Their VP of marketing said they made more on day one than they projected for the entire week.

blocks.text: That last one works because people shop around on Black Friday. They add to cart on Friday, come back Saturday, leave again. If your flow can only reach them once every two weeks, you miss those returns. One thing to do today: find your gross margins per product. If you've entered product costs in Shopify, you'll see them in Shopify analytics. If the numbers scare you, you're probably in the Stack or the Vault.

faq.q: How do I calculate if my Shopify store can afford a Black Friday discount?
faq.a: Use the break-even multiplier: your margin divided by your margin minus the discount. The result is how many times more orders you need just to make the same profit. As a rule of thumb, above a 60% margin you have room to discount, below 50% you don't.

faq.q: What should I offer on Black Friday if my margins are thin?
faq.a: Give away value instead of price. A free gift with a $100 order that the customer sees as worth $30 might cost you about $8, while 10% more off costs you $10 of margin. Gift card bonuses that only work from January and free shipping are other options. If customers also only buy once, sell access with limited products or early access instead of discounting.

faq.q: When should Black Friday early access start?
faq.a: Give your early access list VIP access 48 to 24 hours before everyone else, while all products and variants are still available. Start collecting sign-ups now with a form on your site, your order confirmation page and Instagram keyword replies through Klaviyo. Klaviyo reported Scuffers' early access email made around 400% more revenue than the same email sent to everyone else.

faq.q: How do I give returning customers a separate discount in Shopify?
faq.a: Go to Discounts in Shopify, create a discount, and under Eligibility pick customers who have purchased at least once. That lets you give your regulars an extra gift or an extra 5% that new visitors don't get. New visitors should see reviews, best sellers and your guarantee instead.

faq.q: What abandoned cart settings work best for Black Friday?
faq.a: Send the abandoned cart email faster and allow it more often. Little Sleepies changed the send time from one hour to 30 minutes and let customers receive it once a day instead of once every two weeks, and made more on day one than they had projected for the whole week. Shoppers come back and leave several times over the weekend, so a strict frequency limit misses them.

faq.q: Should I turn off my welcome pop-up during Black Friday?
faq.a: Yes. A "sign up and get 10% off" pop-up is irrelevant when you're running a bigger sale, so turn it off along with any other campaigns running at the same time. Also show the discounted price with the original price crossed out and use automatic discounts so shoppers don't leave checkout to hunt for codes.
